title: Helix Retail — cold outreach cheat sheet and pilot sketch
content:
Purpose: quick personal cheat sheet for outreach to Helix Retail (US regional chain). For first cold sequence + pilot proposal. Keep short, repeatable, low-touch.

Account snapshot (what I can verify quickly):
- HQ: Portland, OR. ~85 stores, mostly urban mall and high-street footprints.
- Business model: POS + fulfillment (BOPIS), in-house personalization team, mid-stage series-B retailer.
- Tech signals: uses BigQuery, Segment, and a custom monorepo -> likely Kubernetes + GKE. Job postings show ML infra + infra engineers (2 roles in last 6 months).
- Pain signals (from investor blog + Glassdoor): heavy cart abandonment during peak events; personalization team stretched; tooling for real-time recommendations is rudimentary.
- Recent news: raised $85M (Series B) in 2025; announced pilot with a payments gateway last quarter -> investing in customer experience.

Why Redwood could fit:
- Use case angle 1: conversational assistant for store associates to pull up SKU info, stock, and suggested alternatives (latency and cost matter; low integration surface with existing POS via API).
- Use case angle 2: real-time product description generation for large catalog where copy is stale (embedding-based similarity + generation -> reduce copy ops & improve SEO/ads).
- Use case angle 3: re-ranking product suggestions at checkout to reduce abandonment (embedding/rerank pipeline; Redwood Optimize + caching could cut token cost and preserve latency SLOs).

Decision maker / outreach map (best guesses):
- Head of Digital / VP ecomm: Rebecca Chen (role listed on press release).
- Head of Personalization / Sr Manager ML: likely someone listed on job postings (reach out via LinkedIn ML infra postings).
- Head of Store Ops (for associate use-case): Jason Morales.
- Champion target: Senior PM on personalization (more likely to advocate for a pilot).

Cold email skeletons (3 variants) — keep concise, value-first:
1) Short technical intro (for ML infra / platform):
Subject: Low-friction inference pilot for Helix product re-ranking
Hi Rebecca — saw Helix invested in personalization efforts after Series B — quick question: if you could cut per-recommendation inference cost by 2–3x while keeping 95th pct latency sub-150ms, would you consider a 4–6-week pilot? We ran that exact workload for a mid-market retailer using Redwood Optimize + prefix caching; cost dropped ~38% and cart conversion lifted 2.1pp. Can I share a 1-pager + 15-min demo?

2) Store-associate angle (ops-friendly):
Subject: Prototype assistant for Helix store teams (no infra lift)
Hi Jason — quick note: built a small prototype for floor associates to fetch SKU details, stock, and recommended swaps via simple API + Slack — zero infra changes, avg response 90ms. Would you be open to a short pilot in 2 stores to measure speed & CSAT?

3) Marketing/merchandising angle (content scaling):
Subject: Automate & scale product copy with safety guardrails
Hey — noticed some catalog items with brief copy — we help teams generate/descriptive copy + human-in-loop approval UI; one retailer reduced copy backlog by 70% in 3 weeks. If Helix cares about SEO + ad costs, worth a quick chat?

Playbook for first touch (email -> LinkedIn -> SDR follow-up):
- Day 0: Send targeted email to VP/Head. Attach single-page pilot memo + 1 slide with expected metrics (cost delta, latency, uplift).
- Day 3: LinkedIn connection note to head + 1-line follow up referencing email.
- Day 7: SDR phone attempt to gatekeeper (ask 2 qualifying Qs).
- If no reply by day 14: send short case study note + ask for intro to ML/product person.

Pilot sketch (4–6 weeks):
- Goal: measure per-recommendation latency & unit cost and impact on 90-day add-to-cart rate (or a proxy like click-through on recommendations).
- Scope options (pick one):
  A) Re-rank checkout recommendations (server-side): ingest product catalog snapshots + candidate generator, use Redwood for scoring/rerank. Instrumented A/B in prod with 10% traffic.
  B) Store-associate assistant (edge-hosted or private): small VPC deployment, connect to POS read-only, Slack integration, 2 stores. Measure avg response time and CSAT.
  C) Content generation pipeline: small batch job to build product descriptions, integrate with content review UI.
- Deliverables: metrics dashboard (latency, cost/kg token, failed requests), short health runbook, rollout checklist, 1 internal training doc for store staff.
- Pricing for pilot (back-of-envelope): free platform credits + $X/day infra (covering dedicated capacity for peak tests) OR revenue-opportunity share depending on measured uplift. Keep it simple: proposed ask = 6 weeks, sign-off from Head of Personalization and Store Ops for the respective scope.

Objection handling (short):
- "We already use [big cloud provider model endpoint]": acknowledge, then ask which SLOs/costs pain them most. Offer a cost/latency snapshot from a quick 48-hour benchmark with no code changes.
- "Security/compliance": highlight Private option (VPC) + KMS support + audit logs; offer low-risk initial pilot with data redaction + synthetic prompts.
- "Internal infra team will not allow new vendors": propose a proof-of-concept run in a sandbox or Dedicated node that IT controls; bring infra lead into planning call early.
- "No product bandwidth": offer to run a 2-week proof where Redwood engineers wire up connectors and instrument metrics; minimal product involvement required for initial signal.
